Shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the southern gateway to the Red Sea and a key maritime chokepoint like the Strait of Hormuz, dropped to its lowest level in months on Sunday after Iran's Houthi rebel allies in Yemen traded fire with Saudi Arabia, according to shipping intelligence firm Kpler.

The Houthis attacked oil installations along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast on Saturday and said their blockade of Saudi ports would remain in effect. The Houthis imposed their blockade last week in response to Saudi attacks on their infrastructure.

Traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb had increased last week, as an alternative route for energy products with the Strait of Hormuz largely gridlocked, but Sunday saw only 11 commodity ships transit the passage, which Kpler said was the lowest level in months.

The disruption to shipping through both straits caused oil prices to jump sharply last week, though the lull in fighting between Iran and the U.S. over the weekend has seen the cost of crude fall again.

Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has not rebounded.
